## Proof

**Setup.** A Norm-Bound Linear Differential Inclusion (NLDI) is the system
$$\dot{x} = Ax + Bp, \qquad q = C_q x + D_{qp} p, \qquad z = C_z x + D_{zp} p,$$
subject to the componentwise norm-bound (sector) constraint
$$p^T p \le q^T q \qquad \text{(i.e., } \|p\|_2 \le \|q\|_2 \text{ for all } t\text{)}.$$
The **output energy** for a given initial state $x(0)$ is the worst-case accumulated output squared norm:
$$\sup_{p(\cdot)\,\text{admissible}} \int_0^\infty z(t)^T z(t)\,dt.$$

**Quadratic Lyapunov approach.** Choose a quadratic Lyapunov function $V(x)=x^T P x$ with $P=P^T>0$. If we can guarantee
$$\dot V(x) + z^T z \le 0 \tag{$\star$}$$
for every $x$ and every $p$ satisfying $p^Tp\le q^Tq$, then integrating from $0$ to $\infty$ (assuming $x(t)\to 0$, which follows from $\dot V\le -z^Tz\le 0$ and standard invariance arguments) gives
$$\int_0^\infty z^T z\,dt \le V(x(0)) - \lim_{t\to\infty}V(x(t)) \le x(0)^T P\, x(0).$$
Hence $x(0)^T P x(0)$ is an upper bound on the output energy. The **smallest upper bound provable via quadratic Lyapunov functions** is obtained by minimizing $x(0)^T P x(0)$ over all admissible $(P,\lambda)$.

**Applying the S-procedure.** Condition $(\star)$ requires
$$f_0(x,p) := 2x^T P(Ax+Bp) + z^Tz \le 0$$
whenever
$$f_1(x,p) := p^Tp - q^Tq \le 0.$$
By the S-procedure, a sufficient (and, for this single-constraint case, necessary) condition is the existence of a scalar $\lambda\ge 0$ such that
$$f_0(x,p) + \lambda\, f_1(x,p) \le 0 \qquad \forall\,(x,p).$$

**Expanding the quadratic form.** Substituting $z=C_z x+D_{zp}p$ and $q=C_q x+D_{qp}p$:

- $z^Tz = x^T C_z^T C_z\, x + 2x^T C_z^T D_{zp}\, p + p^T D_{zp}^T D_{zp}\, p$,
- $q^Tq = x^T C_q^T C_q\, x + 2x^T C_q^T D_{qp}\, p + p^T D_{qp}^T D_{qp}\, p$,
- $2x^T P(Ax+Bp) = x^T(A^TP+PA)x + 2x^T PB\, p$.

Collecting terms, $f_0+\lambda f_1$ is the quadratic form in $(x,p)$ with block matrix

$$\mathcal{M}(P,\lambda) = \begin{bmatrix} A^TP + PA + C_z^TC_z + \lambda\, C_q^TC_q & PB + C_z^T D_{zp} + \lambda\, C_q^T D_{qp} \\[2pt] B^TP + D_{zp}^T C_z + \lambda\, D_{qp}^T C_q & D_{zp}^T D_{zp} + \lambda\,(D_{qp}^T D_{qp} - I) \end{bmatrix} \le 0.$$

**The optimization problem.** The smallest quadratic-Lyapunov-provable upper bound on the output energy is the optimal value of the semidefinite program

$$\boxed{\begin{aligned}
\min_{P,\;\lambda}\quad & x(0)^T P\, x(0) \\[2pt]
\text{s.t.}\quad & P = P^T > 0, \\ & \lambda \ge 0, \\ & \mathcal{M}(P,\lambda) \le 0, \end{aligned}}$$

with **variables**:
- $P \in \mathbb{S}^n_{++}$ — a symmetric positive-definite $n\times n$ matrix (the Lyapunov matrix), and
- $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ — a nonnegative scalar (the S-procedure multiplier).

**Conclusion.** The smallest upper bound on the output energy $\sup \int_0^\infty z^Tz\,dt$ provable via quadratic Lyapunov functions is the optimal value
$$x(0)^T P^\star\, x(0),$$
where $(P^\star,\lambda^\star)$ solves the SDP above. The bound is tight within the class of quadratic Lyapunov functions: any $P$ satisfying the LMI with some $\lambda\ge 0$ certifies the bound $x(0)^TPx(0)$, and minimizing over all such $(P,\lambda)$ yields the least conservative (smallest) bound achievable by this method.
